testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch and:

options.text: Turn on the low pressure warning light.
Turn off the low pressure warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the brake lights.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in an air brake vehicle, air pressure moves an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Stop where you are and park.
Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, you must exit the roadway as soon as safely possible and park. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within:
questions.correctAnswerText: 45 seconds.
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: The best way to use brakes on a steep downhill is to:

options.text: Keep your foot on the brake the entire way down.
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this as you go down the hill.
Use the brakes only near the bottom of the hill.
Press the brake pedal steadily the entire way down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this as you go down the hill.
questions.explanation: On steep downhills, use your brakes only to help the engine do the braking. Apply the brakes to slow down, then release them. When you reach your safe speed, repeat this cycle.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. You should check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical force.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks but have separate hoses and lines.
Both systems use the same hoses and lines.
One system is primary and the second system is a backup if the first one fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share the same brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are located:

options.text: Only on the driver's side wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all four wheels.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are installed at all four wheels. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should:

options.text: Warm up the vehicle to make sure fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Start driving as soon as the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a dual air brake vehicle, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. Watch the air pressure gauges to check the pressure levels.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
Stay open while the vehicle is driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the maximum safe leakage rate is 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove this water and oil.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Air takes time to flow through the air lines to the brakes. There is usually a delay of at least one-half second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes begin to work. This is called brake lag.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: By tapping the brake pedal three times
By pushing in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By pushing in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: The parking brake in air brake vehicles is controlled by a knob. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system has very low pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. If this happens while driving, you should exit the road and park as soon as possible.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.correctAnswerText: The supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: All air tanks must include:
questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve.
questions.explanation: All air brake system tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove water and oil that build up in the tanks. They can be manual or automatic.

questions.question: Service brakes should:

options.text: Only be tested by a trained mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be tested before every trip.
questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before you drive. This helps you find problems before you are on the road.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Hold compressed air for the brakes.
Should be drained of all air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in an air brake system hold compressed air for the brakes to use. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and oil. If these liquids build up in the system, they will damage the brakes.

questions.question: What do the two systems of a dual air brake system share?
questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is pushed down, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if it is warm outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to move through the brake lines. There is a delay of at least half a second between pressing the brake pedal and when the brakes start to work.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Used when transporting both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used when transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to drive a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases. It applies to both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.
